g_roast: Twenty eight years guiding caravans across the Sahara, my guests, and I never once lost a camel the way you lost that map this morning.
In Zagora we have a sign that says Timbuktu, fifty two days. This party would take fifty two days to find the sign.
g_fire_back: Ah, very funny, my friend, from the one who drank half the water on the first day and asked where the well was.
Bismillah, a fair hit, I felt it. The desert teaches all of us, and tonight it's teaching me.
g_pile_on: Worse, my guests, much worse. They walked in a circle for an hour and blamed the sun for moving.
After that they wanted me to find water, standing beside a river, my friends, a very large river.
lines.g_peacemake: Doucement, both of you, gently. Sit, drink some water first, then tea, and then you may argue properly, like civilised people.
lines.g_take_side: Forgive me, but {name} is right this time. The ground says so, not my liking for them.
lines.g_left_out: Talk, both of you, it's fine. I'll check the water skins, somebody always forgets.
lines.g_include: Come, sit, there's always room at a fire for one more guest. Water first, then tea, that's the rule of my house.
lines.g_bad_plan: My plan, my guests. We cross at noon, in the worst heat, with no water and no guide, and we trust the camels to know the way.
lines.g_plan_yes: Yallah, simple and careful, I like it. A plan like that brings a caravan home.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that plan runs out of water before the end, I can see it already. We fix it now, or the desert fixes it for us.
lines.g_hype: Bismillah, my guests, steady now. Drink before you're thirsty, stay together, and we all come out the other side, inshallah.
lines.g_toast: A small toast, with mint tea, poured from high so it sings. To my guests, who share their water without being asked. That's the whole of good manners.
lines.g_cheers: To all of you, my guests, and somebody hold their glass still while I pour.
g_quiet_line: The palm groves along the Draa river at dusk, my friends, and the call to prayer coming across the water. I can still hear it, if I'm quiet.
A clear night like this one, in the desert, you can see so many stars that the sky looks crowded. Here it's nearly as good.
lines.g_after_wipe: Everybody stay down, drink some water, slowly, little sips. Good, everyone breathing, alhamdulillah. Now we rest, and then we go again.
lines.g_crew: For twenty eight years I brought strangers safely across the sand, my guests. You're the first caravan I didn't want to reach the end.
lines.g_exasperated: I said ration the water, three times, very politely. And now I'm holding an empty skin and a very polite face.
lines.g_love_sharp: You read the ground before you step on it, {name}. In the desert that keeps a caravan alive.
lines.g_love_kind: You share your water without being asked, {name}. I look for that in anyone, before anything else.
lines.g_love_funny: You make the whole camp laugh on the hard nights, {name}. That's worth a spare camel, believe me.
lines.g_love_brave: You walk into the poisoned country calmly, {name}, without making a story of it. That's real courage.
lines.g_love_steady: You're patient, {name}, all the time, like the desert itself. I admire that very much.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand a route before I've finished drawing it, {name}. Zagora would have hired you.
lines.g_love_honest: You say plainly what's true, {name}, without decoration. A guide trusts a person like that with his life.
lines.g_love_quiet: You can sit by a fire without needing to talk, {name}. The desert taught me to value that.
lines.g_love_fierce: You'd fight anyone who threatens the young ones, {name}. A father recognises that.
lines.g_love_warm: You make strangers feel like guests, {name}, the moment they arrive. That's the best kind of person.
g_loved: Ah, thank you, my friend, you're very kind. Now have some tea, I insist.
Bismillah, stop, you'll make a guide proud, and pride is bad for a guide.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You search out people's weak places, {name}, like a sandstorm finds a crack in a tent. Leave them be, please.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep offering me your water, {name}, and I keep telling you, a guide drinks last. Let me do my work.
lines.g_hate_funny: A joke, now, {name}? The camel is lame and the well is dry. Later, please, much later.
lines.g_hate_brave: You rush ahead into the dunes, {name}, and call it bravery. The desert will teach you, I hope gently.
lines.g_hate_steady: The light is going while you wait, {name}. In the desert you move at dawn or not at all.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain the desert to me, {name}, after one day in it. Twenty eight years, and I'm still learning.
lines.g_hate_honest: Each hard word leaves you the moment it arrives, {name}. In my house we drink tea first and speak after.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You sulk in silence, {name}, and expect us to know. I read sand, my friend, not hearts.
lines.g_hate_fierce: The wind, the sand, the tea, {name}, you fight all of it. The wind doesn't care, and you only tire yourself.
lines.g_hate_warm: You fill every quiet hour with talk, {name}. A few of us listen to the night, it has things to say.
lines.g_respect: We don't agree, {name}, and we may never. But you shared your water with the slowest one today, and I saw it.
lines.g_call_out: Forgive me, {name}, but that one was yours. We agreed to wait for the cool of the evening, and you went in the heat.
lines.g_stung: Ah, fair, I heard you, and you're right to say it. I'll go and make tea.
lines.g_concede: Alhamdulillah, {name}, you were right and I was wrong. Even an old guide misreads the dunes some days.
lines.g_nod: Shukran, {name}, very kind. Now drink some water.
lines.g_callback_save: You pulled me out of that sandstorm of claws, {name}, when I'd lost my bearings. I owe you a whole caravan.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and I still upright when the rest were down, {name}, both of us dry as old leather. I tell that one at every fire.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me I was being too cautious, I was offended until the evening. Then the weather turned, and you'd have had us home.
lines.g_former_rivals: At first, {name}, I thought you were the kind who'd waste water and blame the well. I was quite wrong about you.
lines.g_changed: I used to keep to myself and the route, my guests. Lately I tell more stories by the fire than I did in twenty years.
g_unguarded: Between us, my friend. I've been away more than I've been home, my whole life, and I'm only now counting what that cost.
Just you and me, so I'll say it. Some nights I walk out past the camp just to hear the wind, because it's the only voice that sounds like home.
lines.g_clipped: As you wish, my guest. I'll be with the wagons.
lines.g_noticed_open: Ah, look at that, a whole story told properly, beginning, middle and end. Please, go on, I'm listening, and the tea is hot.
arg_ask: {player}, my friend, would you settle this? Mine has been said with tea and courtesy, and still we go in circles.
Be our judge, {player}, please. In the desert the eldest decides, but you're wiser than the eldest here.
lines.arg_backed_me: Shukran, {player}, a wise decision. I'll pour you the first glass tonight.
lines.arg_backed_them: So be it, your decision, and I'll respect it. The desert will tell us who was right, inshallah.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You don't take a side, then, like a good host between two guests, and I understand.
lines.arg_always_their_side: They win every time, {player}, every one. I'm a patient man, but even sand keeps count of the wind.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody chooses, so I will, gently. My way, yallah, and we move.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, forgive me, I can't do that. I've refused contracts for less.
lines.arg_grumble: I'll let it rest, my friend, mostly. The desert remembers, and so do I, a little.
lines.arg_settled: Half each, a fair division, like water shared on a crossing. Good, now tea.
lines.seen_listens: My friend {player}, you let people tell their whole story, even when it's long. That's a host's gift, and a rare one.
lines.seen_truth: Like a good guide, {player}, the distance you tell people is the true one, not the hopeful one. That's how caravans survive.
lines.seen_jokes: On the hard nights you have us all laughing, {player}. A caravan pays extra for a traveller like that.
lines.seen_stays_out: A wise host keeps out of his guests' quarrels, {player}, and so do you. I see it.
lines.seen_biased: The best water goes to one guest, {player}, on every crossing, I notice. A guide counts the skins, it's a habit.
lines.seen_harsh: Gently, {player}, because you can be harsh. Some of these people are a long way from home, like the rest of us.
lines.seed_right: The counsel you gave me after that terrible day, {player}, I followed it. It held, the way a well holds in a dry year, and I thank you.
lines.seed_remember: What you said that bad night, {player}, is still with me, like wind on the dunes. I'm still listening to them.
lines.seed_wrong: Your route, {player}, made for a harder crossing. I'm only telling you, without blame.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Sit with me a moment, {player}, and drink something. That was close, and I need a glass of tea and a friend.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: The whole caravan on the ground. Come, sit, and we'll retrace it, like a caravan that lost its way, without blame.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: I was watching the sky when {name} fell, {player}. Reading the danger was my task, and I read the wrong thing.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, everyone safe, alhamdulillah. That's a caravan arriving whole, {player}, and there's no better feeling.
lines.talk_development: A question from your guide, {player}. Do I seem changed? I told a story about myself at the fire, and I never do that.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Tired, {player}, I become very formal and very cold, which {name} has felt lately, though they deserve better.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Is {name} fond of me, {player}, would you say? Or only fond of the tea?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} tries my patience daily, {player}. But in a sandstorm, they're the one I'd hold on to.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} hasn't touched their water today, {player}. That's a sign, in my experience, and not a good one.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Permit me a small observation, {player}. The best supplies keep reaching {name} first. Perhaps there's a reason, and I'd be glad to hear it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Simply, {player}, {name} and I don't travel well together. Pretending otherwise only makes the road longer.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We march into country with no water and no road home, {player}. I've buried men who did that, and I won't do it again.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: My judgement of {name} was poor, {player}. Their eyes were truer than mine, and I'd like that known.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: With respect, {player}, a fair question. The long crossings go out without me. Is it my work, or is it me?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit went to {name}, and I learned it from the empty space in my pack. A word would have been enough, {player}.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Shukran, {player}, my heart is lighter. Now, tea, I insist.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: It will pass, inshallah, like a storm. Give it a night.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: It didn't help, my friend, but thank you for trying. I'll see to the wagons.
lines.talk_lands_development: So others see it. Then it's true, alhamdulillah.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Perhaps, perhaps not. A man can't see his own tracks behind him.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, my friend, I don't think so. You've misread the sand there.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: That's fair, and wise. I'll sit with {name} and talk, over tea.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Perhaps, I can't say. People shift more than dunes.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I spoke, please. And nothing to {name}, I ask you.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, and I accept it with thanks. It stings, but it's fair.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Your words are heard, my friend, and tonight they'll keep me company.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's the way the wind blows. Good to know.
lines.talk_door_closed: That's enough of that for tonight, my friend. I'll be by the fire with the tea.
lines.anchor_notice: You're not the traveller who first came to my fire, my friend. I've watched a thousand people cross the desert, and you've changed the way the good ones do.

history.open: Water first, {player}, please, drink, then we talk. Twenty eight years guiding caravans out of Zagora, at the edge of the Sahara, and I've never let a guest go thirsty.

options.reply: With camels first, then with trucks, which are louder and less wise. The sand moves every night, and you learn to read it like a face.
Everyone says that until the second hour. Drink, please, humour an old guide, and you'll thank me tomorrow.
Ha, no, a camel misses nobody, my friend. But I miss them, the grumpy ones most of all.

history.open: I'm finding a summer route across the Flats, {player}. In the worst heat no caravan can cross now, but there's a way through, and I have most of it. Four more seasons of walking, and I have the seasons.

options.text: Why does it matter so much?
options.reply: Because people are stuck on the far side for half the year, unable to come home. A route is a door, my friend, and somebody always needs a door.

options.text: Can I walk some of it with you?
options.reply: Of course, bismillah, I'd be honoured. Bring water, and patience, and I'll bring the tea.

history.open: My youngest is Nour, {player}. She was nine. My other three are grown, but Nour came late, and she was the light of our house. When she was small she sat on my shoulders at the front of the caravan and told me which way to go.

options.reply: Never, not once, and I always pretended she was. Khadija said I'd ruin her. I hope she's somewhere, ruining somebody else's sense of direction.
Inshallah, my friend. Every caravan I bring across, I look at every child in the back, every single face.

friend.open: When I arrived, {player}, I asked the land for permission in my own language, the way we do before a crossing. And something answered. I felt it in the ground, like a camel kneeling. I've told almost nobody, because people look at you strangely.

options.reply: Shukran, my friend. It's a small thing to hear, and a big thing to me.
Only yes, I think, the way a host says come in. Since then I've tried to be a good guest.

sworn.open: In the desert, {player}, you share your last water only with family. I would share my last water with you, without thinking. That's the most a man from Zagora can say.

options.reply: Then we're family, bismillah, and you'll always have a place at my fire.

options.text: As long as it comes with tea.
options.reply: Ha, always with tea, my friend, poured from high, so it sings.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sat down over tea and settled it properly. All is well now, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Shukran, it's easier to travel with peace in the caravan.
I did, of course, and they held their glass very still, which was the apology.
